hyps.why: Edge 4 starts at node 1, which is unreachable when edge 0 is none, so a conv there adds nothing.
With edge 1 removed, edge 5 can only carry signal via the 0->1->2 route, which limits the benefit of a strong conv on it.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none, so the edit is nearly useless.
The conv on edge 4 cannot receive input when edge 0 is none.
Edge 5's input path is mostly cut when edge 1 is none.
Edge 2 is dead when node 1 receives no input.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv on the direct input-to-output edge adds a whole new path, a bigger gain than replacing another op.
Restoring edge 0 from none to a conv reconnects node 1 and its downstream edges, so the gain is large.
Adding a conv in place of none opens the 0->2 path, giving a larger gain than swapping one real op for another.
Replacing none on the final edge into the output adds a feature path that was missing.
